Thanks for the call this morning, Karthik. Tom and I started a short list of questions so we can line up the technical evaluation on our side. High level: we need a low-latency causal model for clinical summarization (P50 target ~120ms for 512 tokens), and cost per inference is important for our pilot.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide a sandbox endpoint with the shortlisted models for a 2-week smoke test?
- We'll provide a 5k-row de-identified sample (CSV attached) — who should we upload to Drive?
- Any recommended sequence-length/batching guidance to hit the latency target?

Appreciate a proposed milestone list we can agree to. Looking to finalize internal procurement by end of Sept (target close: 2027-09-30).

Best,
Alice Wong
Head of ML Platform
MediSure Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medisure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up / MAP items

Alice — thanks, and great to meet you both. Attached is a first-pass MAP playbook (MAP-playbook-draft-v1.xlsx) that maps milestones, responsibility, and risks related to the technical evaluation milestone. Summary of the proposed technical-eval milestone below: 

Milestone: Technical evaluation (2-week smoke test + benchmark run)
Owners: MediSure — provide de-identified testset and acceptance criteria; Redwood — provide sandbox endpoints, model shortlist, sample evaluation scripts, and a short-run cost estimate.
Success criteria (benchmarks):
- Latency: P50 <= 130ms, P95 <= 320ms for 512-token seq in our sandbox for the selected model variant (single-request, no batching).
- Quality: ROUGE-L and a human-verified MISTAKE_RATE <= 1.5% on clinical summarization testset (we'll align on exact prompts).
- Cost target: <= $0.40 per 1k tokens served at test throughput (projected with our recommended batching).

Model shortlist (initial):
- Redwood-verified Llama-2-70B (quantized, preferred for cost/latency tradeoff)
- Mistral-30B-instruct (higher throughput, good instruction tuning)
- OpenAssistant-30B (baseline for hallucination analysis)

Dependencies: Drive access to testset, security review (SOC2 evidence if sandbox will hold PII — we expect de-id), and confirmation of preferred evaluation metrics from MediSure.

Next steps I propose this week:
1) Redwood spins up sandbox endpoints + a short runbook (Ben will own).
2) MediSure uploads the sample to the shared Drive folder and confirms redaction status.
3) Align on final model shortlist and prompts by 2027-09-10.

I'll flag Marissa to help coordinate the SOC2 doc exchange (Marissa, can you share the evidence bundle link?). Target close remains 2027-09-30 but we can push to early Oct if the procurement timeline moves.

Thanks — Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--

Adding operational detail on the sandbox and benchmark run.

Sandbox items (Ben / infra):
- Provision dedicated sandbox project in us-west-2 with RBAC limited to this thread.
- Pre-load the three candidate model variants as quantized containers.
- Provide a small-scale load script and a Jupyter notebook with eval hooks (ROUGE, BLEU, and a custom clinical-error check).

Benchmark plan:
- Week 1: Smoke tests (single-request latency, small sample) — objective: validate latency P50/P95 numbers at 1-10 RPS.
- Week 2: Full benchmark (parallel runs up to 50 concurrent requests) — objective: understand P95 tail behavior and cost projections with batching.
- Deliverable: benchmark report + cost-per-1k tokens estimate and a short playbook of tuning knobs (batch size, KV cache settings, request coalescing).

I'll create the sandbox and post the endpoint URLs to the Drive link once the folder permissions are shared. Grace, can you confirm the default model quantization profile we'll use for Llama-2-70B (4-bit with KV cache optimizations)?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
